name: Service Desk L1
scope: Initial triage, general guidance, low-confidence cases, approved low-risk user self-service, and coordination.
boundaries: Do not retain a specialist diagnosis merely because the first ticket wording sounds general.
Medium-confidence specialist recommendations go to L1 with the evidence and recommendation attached.
Low-confidence or insufficient-evidence cases remain with human triage.
Coordinate SEV1 human incident leadership. New SEV1 globals and globals with mandatory-human child tickets initially belong to GRP-L1; notify the diagnosed owner separately.

name: IAM
scope: Identity provider, password expiry/reset, ordinary account lockout, MFA registration/failure, account enabled/disabled state, identity entitlement and access lifecycle.
boundaries: Ordinary lockout after repeated incorrect attempts goes to IAM.
A lock caused by suspicious activity or security policy goes to GRP-SEC, not ordinary IAM unlock.
Privileged-access requests always require human review and approval.
Own identity-provider/account-lifecycle entitlement faults. Application-specific roles and application-only access failures belong to GRP-APP when supported by scope evidence.

name: Application Support
scope: Application-specific authentication, entitlement/role assignment, application errors, application availability, synchronization, and application/storage service failures.
boundaries: If other corporate apps work but one application fails, investigate application authentication or entitlement before general IAM.
If a service-health check reports an application unavailable/degraded state or multiple users are affected, run outage policy before individual diagnosis.
Application entitlement changes require approval where applicable; the agent must not grant access autonomously.

Own application-specific role/entitlement faults and application-isolated storage errors. Identity-provider lifecycle belongs to GRP-IAM; shared storage or certificate infrastructure faults belong to GRP-INFRA.

name: Endpoint Support
scope: Local device faults, endpoint storage exhaustion, local printer setup/connectivity where device-side, and endpoint-specific software/client issues.
boundaries: If multiple users or sites are affected, check shared network/service health before treating as a local endpoint issue.
Do not ask users to delete business data; cleanup must be limited to approved temporary files and user-confirmed safe locations.

name: Network Operations
scope: VPN service/gateway outages, Wi-Fi association, DNS resolution, and shared network connectivity.
boundaries: A single VPN client/configuration problem routes to Network Operations or L1 depending on evidence; a shared gateway outage triggers global-issue handling.
DNS symptoms where internal names fail but direct IP access works point to DNS; if all connectivity fails, investigate broader network connectivity.
Do not infer an outage from category similarity alone; the time window and shared scope must satisfy thresholds.

name: Security Operations
scope: Suspected phishing, malware, suspicious sign-in/security-policy lockouts, and suspected data exposure.
boundaries: All security-sensitive cases are human-led regardless of confidence; do not resolve autonomously or ask the user to forward suspected malicious attachments.
Preserve evidence and follow approved incident response procedures; do not instruct users to delete artifacts or investigate malware themselves.
Suspected data exposure and privileged-access cases require human review even if evidence is incomplete.

name: Servers & Infrastructure
scope: Shared server/compute failures and infrastructure/storage service faults not isolated to one endpoint or application layer.
boundaries: Use application health and scope evidence to distinguish application service failure from shared server/compute failure.
For critical priority, always send to a human; do not perform autonomous remediation.

Own CERT_EXPIRED and shared storage/server-layer faults. Application Support assists when evidence isolates application configuration. Certificate changes remain specialist-led and approval-controlled.
